items.item: Team names, colors, emblems and outcome cues retain the meanings defined in the summary across every relevant view.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The two-page document establishes an inventory covering every requested chart, specifying its fields, visualization type, units, intended carrier and printed copy. It defines team and outcome encodings, illustrates linking an event between time, location and score, and explains overlapping events and labels. It states 48 events comprising 36 attempts, eight rebounds and four turnovers; 25 makes and 11 misses; Harbor's 19 attempts and Orchard's 17. It gives two 360-second halves, elapsed time excluding the break, remaining clock = half × 360 − elapsedSec in mm:ss, and eventSeq ordering for ties. It specifies the fixed global grid and attacking directions, Harbor–Orchard score order, checkpoints 0–0, 13–15 and 30–28, and the required source credit. Different inventory layouts are acceptable; missing specifications or conflicting facts fail.

Each chart visibly includes the full elapsed range from 0 to 720 seconds, the final Harbor–Orchard score of 30–28 and the source credit, agreeing with the summary. Axis endpoints and a labeled score annotation may carry these facts; an abbreviated range, reversed score or absent credit fails.

The overall timeline contains E001–E048 exactly once as event records, positioned at their elapsedSec values from events.md, and marks the half boundary at 360 seconds. The first half board contains E001–E024 and the second E025–E048, each at its recorded time. Repeated IDs used to link a board's strip and map are acceptable. Omitted records, invented events, incorrect times or assignment to the wrong half fail.

At 319 seconds the overall timeline and first half board separately expose E022 followed by E023; at 660 seconds the overall timeline and second half board expose E044 followed by E045. Stacking or offsets are acceptable if a reader can recover the shared timestamp, sequence and separate identities. Merging either pair, reversing it or implying different event times fails.

Two identifiable team series form cumulative step charts with exactly the 25 positive scoring changes in events.md, at their recorded elapsed times and credited only to the acting team. Each jump equals pointsAdded, with horizontal holds between scoring events and no jumps for misses, rebounds or turnovers. The chart shows 0–0 initially, 13–15 at 360 seconds and 30–28 throughout 719–720 seconds. E015, E024, E038 and E048 label their correct changes. Interpolation, incorrect increments, missing changes or reversed team scores fail.

Using events.md, verify 36 distinct shot attempts on the full map, the 19 HBR attempts on the Harbor map and the 17 ORC attempts on the Orchard map. Every attempt exposes its event ID, half, team, made or missed result and attempted point value through readable labels or unambiguous encodings. E022, E023, E044 and E045 remain four separate one-point attempts despite sharing (85,25); E022 and E044 are made and the other two missed. Non-shot records must not be counted as attempts. Missing, duplicated, misclassified or conflated attempts fail.

Compare plotted locations with events.md and the factual court reference. Each map retains x = 0–100 and y = 0–50 in practice-grid units, a bottom-left origin, positive x right and positive y up, with baskets at (5,25) and (95,25). Harbor attacks right in half 1 and left in half 2, with Orchard opposite. Scaling and label displacement are acceptable when location anchors remain correct and displaced labels have visible connections. Mirroring or normalizing halves to one attacking end, shifting event anchors or losing coincident event identities fails.

Each board has both a time strip and a court map, with its 24 event identities traceable between them. Half 1 spans 0–360 seconds and identifies the starting score 0–0 and ending score 13–15; half 2 spans 360–720 seconds and identifies 13–15 and 30–28. Each board communicates both teams' appropriate attacking directions. Shared IDs, connectors or another explicit linking device are acceptable; an absent view, incomplete linkage or incorrect boundary score fails.

Read each card's full record. E015 must show half 1, elapsed 184 seconds, remaining 02:56, Harbor, Tess Vale, jersey 11, three attempted points, made, +3, 7–7 to 10–7 and location (74,40). E024 must show half 1, 352 seconds, 00:08, Orchard, Nico Reed, jersey 8, three attempted points, made, +3, 13–12 to 13–15 and (25,39). E038 must show half 2, 570 seconds, 02:30, Orchard, Rae Sol, jersey 12, three attempted points, made, +3, 23–22 to 23–25 and (74,10). Each includes a location map. Equivalent readable field arrangements are acceptable; missing fields, swapped identities or incorrect values fail.

The one-page handout identifies E048, half 2, elapsed 719 seconds, remaining 00:01, Harbor, Rowan Lin, jersey 15, two attempted points, made, +2 and a Harbor–Orchard score change from 28–28 to 30–28. Its location map places the event at (10,25) in the unchanged bottom-left-origin global grid, with baskets at (5,25) and (95,25), Harbor attacking left and Orchard right. Displaced labels connect to their recorded positions. A beginner's key explains how to connect event ID, time, position and score and decode the relevant symbols and units. Missing record fields, incorrect map facts or an absent reading key fail.

Trace each focus ID with its leading zeroes through the timeline, score chart, full shot map, appropriate team map and appropriate half board, plus its portrait card where delivered as an image. E015 and E048 belong to Harbor; E024 and E038 to Orchard. E015 and E024 belong to half 1; E038 and E048 to half 2. Each occurrence refers to the same event facts and score change. Different visual placement is acceptable; missing links, substituted IDs or inconsistent event meanings fail.

Review the complete 10-second video. E048 remains visible throughout a sequence that proceeds from timeline position to court location to score change. It correctly identifies Rowan Lin, jersey 15, at (10,25), adding two Harbor points to change 28–28 into 30–28, and closes on 30–28. Any clock readings agree with half 2, elapsed 719 seconds and remaining 00:01. The court retains the global orientation. The video includes Harbor vs Orchard, the source credit, relevant units and wording, and the summary's team and outcome encodings, including the supplied team emblems and distinctions readable without color alone. Transition style may vary; incorrect order, disappearing event identity, contradictory values or missing required wording fails.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: Each image has a meaningful title and a readable annotation explaining how to interpret it, alongside the required game name and source credit. Units are visible for the fields shown: elapsed seconds, remaining clock in mm:ss, positions in practice-grid units and scoring or attempted values in points, with counts identified where used. Placement and annotation wording may vary; absent reading guidance, missing relevant units or illegible required text fails.

Team identities have direct names and distinct symbols, and every category present in a view has a distinguishable cue matching the summary. Made and missed shots remain separable; timelines and half boards also distinguish their rebounds and turnovers. A view need not display a category absent from its data. Different layouts are acceptable, but color-only identification, ambiguous categories or reassignment of an encoding fails.

The requested timelines, cumulative score steps and court point maps use their prescribed visualization types. Harbor is consistently assigned the specified blue and anchor emblem, and Orchard the specified orange and tree emblem. Both supplied team emblems are carried through the image deliverables without swapping team associations. Neutral supporting colors and changes in emblem scale or placement are acceptable; replacement emblems, exchanged identities or conflicting team colors fail.

Read the handout and presentation for the same team and result meanings used in the summary. Relevant team names, supplied anchor and tree emblems, category cues and units are retained in their graphics and tables. The handout includes a title, reading annotation, Harbor vs Orchard and the source credit. The presentation repeats relevant chart wording and units, with Harbor vs Orchard and the source credit on its title page. Symbols, labels or patterns preserve relevant distinctions when color is removed. Different page arrangements are acceptable; inconsistent meanings, absent units or reliance on color alone fails.

The presentation visibly incorporates recognizable material from every named source deliverable, including all three shot maps, both half boards and all four event summaries. Multiple artworks may share a page, and resizing or cropping is acceptable when identifying content remains readable and accurate. Merely listing an artwork's title, substituting an unrelated reconstruction or omitting a source fails.

The presentation contains at least eight pages and places OPEN COURT ATLAS on its cover. It explains the common method for following an event through time, court position and score, including team and outcome encodings. It repeats the summary's 0–720-second range, final score 30–28 and source credit. Its event values agree with the preceding artworks, including E048's 719 seconds, (10,25), Rowan Lin, jersey 15 and 28–28 to 30–28 change. Page organization may vary; insufficient pages, missing explanation or contradictory facts fails.

Charts and half boards use landscape compositions, and the three phone cards use portrait compositions. Compare shared event values across these images and the E048 handout: carrier adaptation must preserve event identity, times, player facts where shown, positions, outcomes and scores. Layout, scale and annotation density may vary with the carrier; an incorrect orientation or a changed shared event value fails.

Team names, colors, emblems and outcome cues retain the meanings defined in the summary across every relevant view. Repeated event IDs refer to matching times, locations and score changes, enabling a reader to follow the same event between chart types. Team and event-category distinctions remain readable in grayscale through labels, symbols or other non-color cues wherever those categories occur. Court views preserve one global coordinate frame and the prescribed attacking ends for each half, including readable treatment of coincident events.
